responsibilities: you will design, build and deliver analytics and visualisation solutions from end to end, working closely with stakeholders to understand business needs and translate data into actionable insights
You will manage projects, automate data processes and develop interactive dashboards and analytical models that support business outcomes
You will also collaborate with colleagues across global teams, communicate complex technical concepts to diverse audiences and contribute to the ongoing growth of the team's analytics capability

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: design, build and deliver analytics and visualisation solutions from end to end
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: The JD is delivery/capability framed with no explicit testing, quality, or governance language, and no explicit velocity/speed language either, so it lands as mixed by default lack of strong signal either way.
evidence.domain_risk: global financial services group operating in 30 markets
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Financial services sector implies elevated risk by default, but the JD's own language is generic delivery/analytics framing with no explicit financial-reporting or regulatory override language, so moderate.
evidence.data_team_maturity: help develop analytics capabilities ranging from business intelligence and interactive dashboards to advanced quantitative models
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: An existing global analytics team already delivers BI and quantitative models and is growing into new areas like AI, indicating an established but scaling function rather than a from-zero build.
evidence.jd_authorship: design, build and deliver analytics and visualisation solutions from end to end, working closely with stakeholders
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Some named tools appear (SQL, Python/R, Power BI, Tableau, AWS/GCP) but the responsibilities themselves are phrased generically without volume/scale specifics, a mix of precise and boilerplate language.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: partners with a wide range of business teams to deliver data-driven insights
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The team explicitly serves a wide range of business functions without naming a single dominant audience, so mixed.
evidence.autonomy_level: you will help develop analytics capabilities
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The framing is supportive/contributory ('help develop', 'support business outcomes') rather than defining direction, so execution.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: AI/ML is mentioned only as a capability area the team is growing into, not a skill expected of the candidate to use or build infrastructure for.
evidence.testing_framing: No testing or data quality signal anywhere in the JD.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: No testing, data contracts, or data quality language appears anywhere in the responsibilities or requirements.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: The JD is framed entirely in delivery/capability terms with no risk, compliance, or reliability register.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: develop analytics capabilities ranging from business intelligence and interactive dashboards to advanced quantitative models
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The team already has established BI and quantitative modelling capabilities that the role extends and grows rather than builds from scratch.
evidence.work_arrangement: Hybrid and flexible working arrangements, dependent on role
